payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_revert.py::test_the_second_subset_never_changes_what_revert_decides stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/gates/core/revert.py. The claim was "The second subset never changes `revert`'s status, failures or tool, except that a checkout or restore that fails is `error`. The witness takes seven first-run outcomes, and a diff that adds no new test. These are a pass verdict, a fail verdict, an errored run and a run that did not enumerate. They are also failures keyed on something other than a name, a handed name left unaccounted for, and a raised exception. It crosses each with eight second-run outcomes. These are one test passing, all passing, all failing, an errored run and a raised exception. They are also a run that did not enumerate, failures keyed elsewhere and every name uncollected. Each result matches the same call without `locations`, which runs only the first subset. A checkout that fails and a restore that fails each give `error`, with no failures and no tool, with a first subset and without one. A first subset that exemption empties still lets the second subset run. That call runs the second subset alone, matches the call without `locations` and carries the clause.". Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_revert.py::test_each_verdict_after_the_reverted_run_carries_the_advisory, and the criterion's witness did not fail.
